mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation, prompting the Fed to raise rates and depressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below 97 for three consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST of more than 1% indicates a broad-based fall in demand for goods and housing, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in CPIAUCSL above 0.5% while FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three months signals unmet inflation expectations despite loose policy, which erodes real equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 0.5% for three months AND FEDFUNDS < 2%
regime_hint: loose monetary policy with rising inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% while UNRATE remains below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals strong job growth but weak wage pressure, which supports corporate margins and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% AND UNRATE < 3.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between monthly increases in RSAFS and subsequent positive S&P 500 5-day returns, as rising consumer savings translate into increased discretionary spending and higher corporate revenues.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly RSAFS increases and positive 5-day S&P 500 returns falls below 0.3 or is not statistically significant in rolling 24-month windows.
